title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-27
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: 근로자 계약 건은 이사님과 재면담 계획 확정 후 본사 회신, 소방 정비 견적 미수 → 담당자에게 추가 업체·새 기한, 금요일 주간 보고 2건, 운송사 조항 회신 확인·링크 재발송.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Friday, November twenty-seventh. It is the last working day before the weekend, so it is a day of weekly reports and deadlines.

Here is the plan for the next twenty minutes. There are eight parts. Part one is this opening. Part two is the top three tasks for today. Part three is the reports you need to collect. Part four is the replies you owe. Part five is your schedule and deadlines. Part six is English review. Part seven is a short role-play. Part eight is the closing.

First, what you finished yesterday. my director said OK to the new KPI plan for next year. KPI means key performance indicator. You sent the new KPI form to all team leaders. You closed a small tax case, and my director said OK to your report. You chose the first supplier for the belt of the fusing machine, and you asked another supplier for one more quote. You asked the warehouse manager to check the buyer names in the fabric stock. You asked the maintenance clerk for the December machine rental list. And you approved two requests for outside workers for loading and unloading. That is a good day of work.
Let's begin.
Part two. Top three for today.
Number one. The worker's contract. Head office made a decision.

What is it? This is the sewing worker whose contract ends in January. You asked head office for an indefinite contract, because she will soon go on leave. Yesterday a head office manager wrote back. Top management does not allow an indefinite contract. They want the case closed, with extra support for the worker. Then a head office compliance manager wrote twice. He talked with my director by phone. He suggests three steps. First, talk with the worker again, and offer extra support. Second, if she does not agree, ask a local legal expert. Third, prepare for a complaint to the labor office or to a buyer.

Why does it matter? This is a sensitive case. If the worker feels forced, the risk becomes bigger. A complaint can reach the labor office or the buyer. So every step must be careful, fair, and written down.

Your first action today: talk with my director this morning. Agree on who meets the worker, and when. Ask the HR manager to join the meeting. Do not promise anything in the meeting until the offer is approved. Then reply to the head office managers with the plan and the date.
Number two. The fire system maintenance. The final quotations did not come.

What is it? You asked the compliance officer for two final quotations by yesterday, on the same conditions. She answered in the afternoon. One supplier refused to give a quotation. The other supplier did not reply. Instead, she checked other factories. They pay much less. But their contracts are different. Some of them only test the equipment. They do not do real maintenance. Another one only covers the fire alarm.

Why does it matter? The fire police check more strictly now. Today we only check the fire extinguishers. The pumps, sprinklers and emergency lights also need yearly maintenance. And without a contract, it is hard to find someone to repair the equipment quickly.

Your first action today: reply to the compliance officer. Ask her to find one or two more suppliers, with the same conditions as before. Also ask her a clear question. Do the cheaper contracts give a maintenance report that the fire police accept? Set a new deadline, for example next Thursday.
Number three. Friday reports.

What is it? Two weekly reports go out today. A weekly finance report goes to head office. And the outsourcing usage report goes to my director. For the outsourcing report, the export manager updates the shared sheet this morning. There is also good news. Yesterday a head office manager replied about the repair suppliers. He said it is fine if we can explain the work as inside work during an audit. He also said to work with the export manager and the chief accountant to fill any gaps.
Why does it matter? These two reports have fixed dates. my director and head office expect them every Friday.

Your first action today: at ten o'clock, check that the export manager updated the shared sheet. Then prepare the outsourcing report in the afternoon. Before you send it, ask the export manager and the chief accountant one question. Do our repair documents fully support inside work?
Part three. Reports to collect.

First, from the export manager. There are three items. The container truck price comparison from several companies is due today. The standard clause replies from the trucking companies were due yesterday. I could not find them in your inbox. Also, she wrote that she cannot open the link in your email about the trucking process. You can say: "I will resend the link now. Could you also send me the replies from the trucking companies today?"

Second, from the fabric warehouse manager. The stock file update is due today. And the buyer check of the fabric stock is due on Tuesday, December first. You can say: "Could you send me the updated stock file by five PM today?"
Third, from the maintenance clerk. The December machine rental list is due today. You can say: "Could you send me the December rental list today, so that I can check it before the month starts?"

Fourth, from the purchasing staff. There are four items. a new manager's Tet tickets. a leaving manager's flight purchase request, which is due today, because he must leave Vietnam by Sunday. The firewood supplier research. And the delivery date from the first supplier for the belt. She often needs a reminder, so ask early. You can say: "Could you update me on these four items by noon?"
Fifth, from the maintenance leader. He also got the the first supplier email. Please check the delivery date with him too.
Sixth, from another supplier. You asked for a quote for the same belt by the end of this week. If another supplier is cheaper, the supplier may change. No action now. Just check your inbox.

Seventh, from the compliance officer. The official letter from the ward for the environmental registration. You asked her to keep asking for it. You can say: "Is there any news from the ward about the official letter?"
Part four. Replies I owe.
First, to the head office managers, on the worker's contract. A good first sentence is: "Thank you for the guidance. We will talk with the worker again next week, and I will report the result."

Second, to the compliance officer, on the fire maintenance. A good first sentence is: "Thank you for checking with the other factories. Please find one or two more suppliers under the same conditions."
Third, to the export manager. Resend the trucking process link. A good first sentence is: "Sorry, please try this new link."

Fourth, to a head office manager, on the utility bills. She asked for the October bills and invoices by Monday, November thirtieth. Ask the purchasing staff to collect them today. You can say to the purchasing staff: "Please send me the October utility bills by Saturday."
Fifth, to the head office manager. A short thank you is enough. A good first sentence is: "Thank you for your advice. We will check the documents with our export manager and chief accountant."
Sixth, the sample export fine. my director said OK. Now you need to talk with the sales team about the cost. That can wait until next week.
Part five. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Friday the twenty-seventh. At eleven o'clock, outside workers unload fabric boxes. At eleven forty-five, there is the battery collection event with the compliance officer, if it is confirmed. A weekly finance report and the outsourcing report go out today. the warehouse manager's stock file, the maintenance clerk's rental list, the truck price comparison, and a leaving manager's flight request are also due.
Saturday the twenty-eighth. The monthly stock status update for head office planning. a manager's answer about the shared PC is due. the HR manager also checks the organization chart.
Sunday the twenty-ninth is a leaving manager's last day to leave Vietnam.
Monday the thirtieth. At nine o'clock, outside workers load an export shipment. The October utility bills go to a head office manager. The weekly firewood report is also due.
Tuesday, December first. the warehouse manager's buyer check of the fabric stock is due.
Wednesday, December second. the compliance officer sends the waste contract data. the export manager sends the cargo insurance quotes.
Part six. English review.
Let's review nine expressions. Four are from yesterday, three are from four days ago, and two are from one week ago.

Number one. The expression is "explore." It means to look into a way or a chance. For example, "Since the trucking companies have no cargo insurance, we would like to explore buying it ourselves." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Since the trucking companies have no cargo insurance, we would like to explore buying it ourselves.

Number two. The expression is "commit." It means to promise that you will do something. For example, "Please do not commit to any clause until I decide." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please do not commit to any clause until I decide.

Number three. The expression is "disrupt." It means to cause problems for a plan or a job. For example, "A late schedule change disrupts the outside workers and other shipments." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. A late schedule change disrupts the outside workers and other shipments.

Number four. The expression is "The same applies to something." It means, this rule is also true for that. For example, "Please send me the draft before you send it to the company. The same applies to the other companies." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please send me the draft before you send it to the company. The same applies to the other companies.

Number five. The expression is "criteria." It means the rules we use to judge or choose. For example, "The old KPI form had no clear criteria for setting targets." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. The old KPI form had no clear criteria for setting targets.

Number six. The expression is "streamline." It means to make a process or a form simpler. For example, "I streamlined the ledger so that it is easier to fill in." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. I streamlined the ledger so that it is easier to fill in.

Number seven. The expression is "To prevent something from happening again, please..." It means, so that this does not happen again, please do this. For example, "To prevent the certificates from expiring again, please add the expiry dates to the training plan." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. To prevent the certificates from expiring again, please add the expiry dates to the training plan.

Number eight. The expression is "rationale." It means the reason behind a decision. For example, "Please explain the rationale for the change for each style." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please explain the rationale for the change for each style.

Number nine. The expression is "I'm not in a position to do something until..." It means, I cannot do it yet. First I need something. For example, "I'm not in a position to approve the plan until you explain each style." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. I'm not in a position to approve the plan until you explain each style.
Good. Today you can use number seven with the compliance officer, and number nine in the worker's case.
Part seven. Role-play.
The situation: this morning, you go to my director's office. You talk about the worker's contract and the plan for next week. Listen first.
Anthony: Good morning. Do you have five minutes? It is about the worker's contract.
Director: Yes, come in. I talked with the compliance manager yesterday.
Anthony: Yes, he sent me his opinion. Head office wants to close the case, with extra support.
Director: Right. So what is your plan?
Anthony: First, the HR manager and I will meet the worker again next week. We will explain the offer clearly and fairly.
Director: Good. And if she does not agree?
Anthony: Then we will ask a local legal expert before we do anything else. We should not force her to agree.
Director: I agree. A forced agreement is a bigger risk.
Anthony: Also, I'm not in a position to make an offer until the offer is approved. Could you confirm it with head office?
Director: OK. I will call a head office manager today.
Anthony: Thank you. I will write down every meeting, so that we have a clear record.
Director: Good. Keep me updated.
Now, let's practice two key sentences.

Sentence one. "I'm not in a position to make an offer until the offer is approved." Say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. I'm not in a position to make an offer until the offer is approved.

Sentence two. "We should not force her to agree, so we will ask a local legal expert first." Say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. We should not force her to agree, so we will ask a local legal expert first.
In the role-play, the director calls head office himself. That is only an example. You decide the real steps with him.
Part eight. Closing.

Today has three main tasks. First, agree on the plan for the worker's contract with my director, and reply to head office. Second, ask the compliance officer to find more fire maintenance suppliers, with a new deadline. Third, send the weekly finance report and the outsourcing report.
If you remember only one thing, remember this. The worker's case needs a careful plan today, so talk with my director first, before you reply to head office.
You are ready. Have a good Friday, Anthony, and see you on Monday.
